objective: test whether point-in-time NOAA GFS temperature forecasts add net return information beyond contemporaneous Kalshi prices

source_contract.forecast_origin: NOAA NCEP GFS global operational model
source_contract.forecast_access: Open-Meteo Previous Runs API fixed-lead archive
source_contract.observations: NOAA NCEI Daily Summaries at the settlement station
source_contract.availability: daily forecast is usable only after every hourly value in its local target day is published, with a conservative six-hour model lag
source_contract.calibration: expanding settlement-station forecast errors by high/low and lead; only observations whose assumed availability precedes the forecast feature are used
source_contract.entry: historical last print plus a two-cent spread reserve and taker fee; calibration proxy, not a fill claim
source_contract.benchmark: matched period x decision label x high/low x side x entry-price bucket market-only return
source_contract.deployment: historical qualification permits shadow monitoring only

families.mechanism: the calibrated forecast distribution differs from the executable market probability
forecast-market disagreement varies by settlement station
forecast information is incorporated differently across contract price regimes
public forecast information is incorporated more slowly when the last market print is stale
the market underreacts when the calibrated weather probability changes between registered horizons

audit_amendments.reason: Feasibility dry run found that daily-temperature contracts are not listed at T-3d. Impossible T-3d level cells and T-3d-to-T-1d revision cells were removed before interpretation; the dry-run result was invalidated and recomputed.

Forecast-versus-observation audit, without Kalshi outcomes, found persistent station bias. Expanding calibration was changed from pooled to settlement-station-specific; on the common out-of-sample forecast set RMSE improved from 4.88F to 4.73F. The dry-run result was invalidated and recomputed.
